query: For high-entropy alloys intended for harsh corrosive mechanical environments, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs resistance to simultaneous wear and corrosion, and why? Propose a controlled comparison that would test the hypothesis, predict how combined degradation and its wear and corrosion components would differ from a matched baseline, define where the prediction should hold or fail, identify supporting prior evidence, and state an observation that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: In high-entropy alloys, a high density of fine, stable grain boundaries promotes the formation of a rapidly self-healing, multicomponent passivating oxide layer that suppresses both corrosion and wear by accommodating localized deformation and blocking corrosive attack at damage sites.
generation.material_initial_state: A high-entropy alloy with a homogeneous elemental distribution and moderate grain size, lacking any preformed passivating surface layer.
generation.intervention: Expose the alloy to a controlled environment where it is simultaneously subjected to mechanical wear (e.g., sliding contact or abrasion) and corrosive attack (e.g., chloride-rich aqueous solution at elevated temperatures).
generation.conditions: Test conditions include a temperature of around 80–100°C, a corrosive chloride-containing aqueous medium under neutral-to-slightly alkaline pH, and cyclic mechanical stress (sliding or repeated impact) applied for a specified duration (e.g., 24–48 hours).
generation.structural_mediator: The grain boundary density and the resulting passivating oxide film that forms selectively along these boundaries.
generation.mechanism: The fine-grained microstructure increases the proportion of high-energy grain boundaries, which serve as nucleation sites for a protective, multicomponent oxide. This oxide layer can self-heal under mechanical wear, reducing the exposure of the underlying alloy to corrosive attack and simultaneously improving resistance to abrasive damage by arresting crack initiation and propagation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to a matched baseline alloy with a coarser or less uniform grain structure (and hence less continuous or robust oxide layer), the high-grain-boundary alloy will show lower wear volume and reduced corrosion rates. The synergy is expected to manifest as a combined degradation rate that is lower than the sum of the individual rates observed when wear and corrosion occur separately.
generation.baseline: A high-entropy alloy sample processed to have a coarser microstructure, resulting in fewer grain boundaries and a less robust passivating oxide film.
generation.boundary: This prediction holds under conditions where the ambient environment supports passivation (e.g., sufficient oxygen availability and moderate corrosivity). It may fail in extremely reducing environments or at very high mechanical stresses where the protective oxide film cannot reform quickly enough.
generation.uncertainty: Exact quantitative improvements in wear and corrosion resistance are uncertain and may vary with the precise alloy composition, processing parameters, and the details of the mechanical and chemical testing conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of high-entropy alloy samples: one with a refined, high grain boundary density (achieved via severe plastic deformation or similar processing) and another with a coarser microstructure. Subject both sets to simultaneous wear-corrosion testing in a chloride solution at 80–100°C with controlled sliding contact. Measure the evolution of surface oxide formation and microstructural changes during testing.
measurements: Surface oxide composition and thickness (using XPS or TEM)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the finely grained alloy does not exhibit a statistically significant reduction in wear volume and corrosion rate compared to the coarser microstructure alloy, or if no stable passivating oxide layer is observed preferentially along grain boundaries, then the hypothesis would be falsified.
